chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man has wealth that is due to his companion. Can he sell him a pearl worth one hundred dirhams for one thousand dirhams, and delay the payment from him to a specified time?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem. My father instructed me to do so, and I did that.' And he claimed that he asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about it, so he said to him the same.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell an item for a higher price if payment is delayed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* validates the permissibility of *bay' al-mu'ajjal* (deferred payment sale), where the seller retains ownership until full payment, a mechanism often used in *bai' al-kali'* or buy-back structures. The Imam’s reference to his father, Imam Al-Sadiq, underscores the continuity of this commercial ruling within the Ahl al-Bayt’s jurisprudence, distinguishing it from *riba* (usury) by ensuring the price reflects the time value of money without interest on debt. This ruling provides a foundational basis for modern Islamic finance instruments involving asset-backed deferred sales.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abdullah, from his uncle Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man who happens to have the wealth for him which had become due upon his companions. Can he sell him a pearl at a fixed price of one hundred Dirham for a thousand Dirhams, and he delays the wealth from him to a specified time?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem. My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> had instructed me<sup>asws</sup> such, so I<sup>asws</sup> did that’. 
And he (the narrator) claimed that he had asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to him similar to that’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn ‘Abd Allah from his uncle, Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man to whom someone owes a certain amount of goods and payback time becomes due. His party sells to him a pearl worth a hundred dirham for a thousand dirham and extends the payback time to another appointed time. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful. My father commanded me to do so and did such a deal.’ He (the narrator) thinks that he had asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it and he (the Imam) had given a similar answer.”
